subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw add a subagent-specific persisted breaker now, fold this into a broader session/tool failure-recovery contract, or defer to existing guards?
rationale: The source gap is real, but code alone cannot choose the permanent failure taxonomy, persistence owner, default enablement, cooldown or half-open behavior, and operator recovery surface.

options.title: Design Bounded Subagent Breaker
options.body: Define a narrow subagent breaker keyed by agent and task signature with typed failure classes, cooldown or half-open state, reset or override behavior, and status surfacing.

options.title: Fold Into Unified Health Receipts
options.body: Treat this as part of a broader session/tool health receipt model shared with #62615, #75923, and #78865 before implementing subagent-specific policy.

options.title: Defer To Existing Guards
options.body: Leave subagent reliability to depth, active-child, timeout, loop-detection, and orphan-recovery controls, accepting that repeated failed respawns remain an operator-managed case.

recommendation.title: Design Bounded Subagent Breaker
recommendation.body: Define a narrow subagent breaker keyed by agent and task signature with typed failure classes, cooldown or half-open state, reset or override behavior, and status surfacing.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across sessions_spawn, registry, docs, and current adjacent guard code.
